findings.text: Host resume snapshot keeps cached control registers three and four, FS and GS bases, stack pointer and selectors for FS, GS and task state, with DS and ES selectors only on 64 bit builds where cached control values may differ from live hardware. Companion shadow cache mirrors entry, exit, pin and execution controls including secondary and tertiary words for change detection without hardware access.

Loaded VMCS descriptor aggregates current and shadow regions, owning CPU number, launched flag, NMI unmasked knowledge, timer soft disable, software virtual NMI block level with entry and blocked timing, MSR bitmap pointer, per CPU linkage, and embedded host snapshot plus shadow controls.

Nested VMCS image is a packed migration stable record opening with hardware header, abort code, launch indicator and reserved growth words, followed by address and control quadwords for IO bitmaps, MSR handling, TSC adjustments, APIC pages, posted interrupts, EPT pointers, EOI maps, exit bitmaps, physical address, link pointer, debug, patrol, performance, page tables, bound config, function controls, EPT list, PML and exiting maps, then 64 bit natural width images of masks, shadows, qualification, linear address and guest plus host registers including segment bases, debug, stack, instruction pointer, flags, sysenter and CET state, then 32 bit controls and status for execution, exceptions, exits, entries, interrupts, limits, access rights, activity and timers, then 16 bit selectors and identifiers ending with PML index, with explicit reserved padding between groups.

Trust domain creation bundle is a packed 1024 byte aligned record holding attributes, extended features, maximum virtual CPU count with six reserved bytes, EPT controls, configuration flags, TSC frequency with thirty eight reserved bytes, six element measurement configuration, owner and owner configuration arrays with four reserved quadwords, and a trailing union viewing the tail either as a flexible CPUID list or as 768 reserved bytes.
CPUID value entry carries four 32 bit register images for leaf results in packed form without internal padding.
When the TDX enable marker is cleared the domain and virtual CPU containers hold only their generic counterparts and expose no extra members.

Field identifier construction places a non architectural marker at bit 63, an 8 bit class at bit 56, and a 32 bit field number in the low bits, with one constructor clearing the marker and another setting it. VMCS, guest state, non architectural guest state and management helpers each bind a fixed class to the appropriate constructor.
Execution controls class identifier is seventeen. Virtual CPU state classes are zero for VMCS, sixteen for guest general registers, seventeen for other guest state, and thirty two for management.

TSC offset and multiplier control indices are ten and eleven. Non architectural details index is 256 with interrupt pending shown by bit zero. Pending NMI management index is eleven. Extended exit qualification type uses the low four bits with value six meaning pending EPT violation. Architectural CPUID metadata identifier is 0x9410000300000000 and measurement extension works in 256 byte chunks.

Maximum guest physical address width flag is bit zero and no RBP modification flag is bit two. TSC frequency expressed in 25 MHz units converts to kilohertz by multiplying by twenty five thousand, with allowed range from one hundred thousand to ten million kilohertz.

Secure EPT entry info encodes level in the low three bits and lifecycle state in bits eight through fifteen recoverable by masking then shifting down by eight. Lifecycle codes are zero free, one blocked, two pending, three pending blocked and four present. Topology enumeration support is bit twenty of features zero metadata.

VMCS encoding distinguishes full versus high halves by bit zero and encodes width in bits thirteen to fourteen for sixteen bit, sixty four bit, thirty two bit and natural width variants. Field table index spans bits one through nine with shift one. Width ordering is sixteen bit zero, sixty four bit one, thirty two bit two and natural three.

In this 64 bit only mode high half accesses are rejected at build time when the field number is constant, natural width is treated as 64 bits, and accessor size is limited to sixteen, thirty two or sixty four bits with each required to match the encoded width for constant fields.

Per width state accessors check the width class before delegating to host read or masked write services and call dedicated failure reporters on error, with reads producing zero on failure. Bit set passes the same bit as value and mask while bit clear passes zero value with the bit as mask. Management and non architectural state checks accept all inputs here.

Exit information predicates distinguish undefined opcode, general protection and device not available by exception vector, recognize single byte breakpoint traps by private software exception type, and recognize asynchronous interrupts by external interrupt type.

Sixteen bit rotation combines a left shift with the complementary right shift constrained to sixteen bits. Shadow field markers for read only and read write expand to no operation. Header guards and the TDX enable marker are fixed constants with TDX disabled, and log prefixes prepend the module name.
Offset lookup storage for nested VMCS fields and its element count are visible outside their defining file as read mostly data initialized from a constant init time list.

Supported field enumeration maps each named control or register to its container byte offset via encoding to index conversion, with 64 bit names occupying paired low and high slots where the high slot is four bytes past the low slot.
Nested VMCS revision tag is 0x11e57ed0 and its image size aliases the standard nested VMX VMCS state size. Natural width is a 64 bit alias to keep migration stable across host widths.
Launch indicator starts cleared after clear and becomes set after first launch. Secure EPT entries cycle among free, pending, present and blocked forms including a combined pending blocked form.

VM read error trampoline preserves general and argument registers, forwards stacked field and fault values to a second stage handler, forces the stacked fault result to zero, then restores registers and returns, with extra argument saves on 64 bit builds.

Failed state reads are indistinguishable from legitimate zero results and failed writes provide only reporting without retry. Forcing the fault result to zero discards the original fault detail. Cached host control images are permitted to diverge from live hardware.
